cheeseburger-on-white-bun-1-large-patty.title: Cheeseburger on white bun with large patty

content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger on a white bun with a large patty consists of a soft white bun, a juicy 167 g beef patty, melted cheese, lettuce, tomato, pickles, onion and sauce. It is a classic fast‑food item popular worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the 1920s in the United States.
A white bun provides a neutral base that lets the cheese and meat flavors shine.
A 167 g patty is considered “large” in most fast‑food chains.
The cheese‑on‑meat melt creates a characteristic “melt‑flow” effect.
Cheeseburgers are often used in advertising as a symbol of American culture.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty supplies high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron and zinc, which support immune function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef provides vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, aiding energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Lettuce, tomato and pickles contribute a modest amount of dietary fiber for digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A cheeseburger can contain 500–800 kcal, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: Cheese and meat contain saturated fats and salt, which may raise cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Melted cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Potential meat pathogens
items.content: Undercooked patty may harbor bacteria; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding the bun. You can add extra sauces, split it in half for easier handling, or enjoy it with a side of fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared cheesburger in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours in an airtight container. For longer storage, reheat to an internal temperature of 71 °C. Freezing is best done without the bun, then reassemble before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey divan is a baked casserole made with finely chopped poultry, a creamy sauce, cheese, and often rice or pasta. The dish has a tender flavor, silky texture, and is typically layered to resemble a “divan.”

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “divan” comes from the French word for a layered dish.
The original recipe often used chicken liver, but modern versions substitute lean meat.
The dish became popular in the United States in the 1950s as a convenient way to use leftover boiled meat.
A golden crust is usually achieved with a mixture of breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan.
Turkey versions are considered more diet‑friendly because turkey is lower in fat than chicken.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Poultry contributes iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: When rice or pasta is used in moderation, the dish fits moderate‑carbohydrate diets.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The grated cheese topping adds calcium, beneficial for bone strength.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cream sauce and cheese can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt; low‑sodium alternatives are recommended.

items.title: Risk of over‑consumption
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑dense due to cream and cheese, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Poultry must be cooked thoroughly to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Sauté finely chopped chicken or turkey until golden, add a creamy sauce (butter, flour, milk), stir in cooked rice or pasta, place in a baking dish, top with grated cheese and bake 20‑30 minutes at 180 °C until a golden crust forms.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the finished divan to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: Cranberry juice drink is a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage made from concentrated cranberry juice, water, and a touch of sugar. It is exceptionally high in vitamin C (5332 mg per serving) and has a characteristic tart‑sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cranberries contain more vitamin C than any citrus fruit.
Traditionally, cranberry juice is used in North American cuisine for sauces and marinades.
Cranberries naturally contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.
Cranberry juice is often recommended for urinary tract health.

items.title: High vitamin C content
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Flavonoids and proanthocyanidins in cranberries protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Urinary tract support
items.content: Proanthocyanidins prevent bacteria from adhering to the bladder walls.

items.title: Cardiovascular benefits
items.content: Cranberry polysaccharides help improve lipid profiles and may lower blood pressure.

items.title: High acidity
items.content: The acidity can irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even a small amount of added sugar may be a concern for those monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Cranberry allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible allergic reactions to cranberry products.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve chilled as a refreshing drink, add to smoothies, cocktails, or use as a base for fruit punches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.

content.title: About
content.content: A chocolate‑filled crepe is a thin pancake made from flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt, lightly fried until golden and then stuffed with a rich chocolate ganache. This dessert is popular in cafés and patisseries, often served with fresh berries, whipped cream or ice cream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crepes originated in France in the 17th century and were originally called “crêpes”.
Chocolate filling is usually made from dark chocolate melted with cream, giving it a silky texture and deep flavor.
In some countries the crepes are flavored with orange zest or a splash of Grand Marnier liqueur.
Crepes can be adapted for dietary needs by using gluten‑free flour or plant‑based milks.
Traditionally crepes are rolled, but they can also be folded into triangles or folded like an envelope.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates in the batter provide quick glucose for energy, useful before activity or after exercise.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium from milk
items.content: Milk in the batter supplies calcium essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Eggs and milk add complete protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs contain B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that aid metabolism.

items.title: Milk and egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy or eggs may experience reactions after eating crepes.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Chocolate ganache often contains added sugar, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of batter and chocolate makes the dish energy‑dense; over‑consumption can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional wheat flour contains gluten, which is problematic for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve warm chocolate‑filled crepes rolled or folded into triangles. Garnish with berries, a dusting of powdered sugar, whipped cream, or a scoop of ice cream. For a lighter taste, use dark chocolate with a high cocoa percentage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked crepes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Store the chocolate filling in a separate jar in the fridge for 5‑7 days. Reheat crepes briefly in a dry pan or microwave before serving to restore softness.

content.title: About
content.content: The powdered fruit flavored drink is a sugar‑free beverage intended to be reconstituted with water. It contains natural‑taste flavorings, low‑calorie sweeteners and added vitamins, but no caloric carbohydrates, making it suitable for diet plans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The powder format allows long‑term storage without flavor loss.
Diet versions often use stevia or sucralose instead of sugar.
Fruit flavors are derived from concentrated extracts rather than real juice.
The product is lightweight and convenient for travel, camping, or office use.
Some brands fortify the drink with B‑vitamins and vitamin C.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Added electrolytes help replenish salts lost during exercise or heat exposure.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Absence of sugar makes the drink suitable for reducing overall caloric intake.

items.title: Vitamin boost
items.content: Vitamin C and B‑complex vitamins aid immune function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: The powder dissolves quickly in water, ideal for on‑the‑go consumption.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Most formulations are free of gluten, safe for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Allergy to flavorings
items.content: Some artificial flavorings may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Artificial sweetener content
items.content: Excessive intake of stevia or sucralose can cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Lack of real fruit
items.content: The powder does not replace whole fruits, so a varied diet remains important.

items.title: Dissolution issues
items.content: Using very cold water may leave residue; warm or hot water ensures complete dissolution.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix one serving (typically 1–2 teaspoons) with 200–250 ml of water, stir until fully dissolved. It can also be added to smoothies or protein shakes for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container. After opening, use within 3–6 months, keeping the powder free from moisture and clumps.

content.title: About
content.content: Nutritional powder mix, light (Muscle Milk) is a protein drink in dry powder form designed for muscle recovery and growth after training. It contains high‑quality whey protein, minimal sugar, and added vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product is developed by Muscle Milk, a well‑known sports nutrition brand.
The light version has fewer calories and carbs than classic protein blends.
Enzymes are included to enhance protein absorption.
The powder dissolves easily in water, milk, or plant‑based drinks without clumping.
Suitable for athletes as well as anyone looking to increase protein intake.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: One serving provides about 20‑25 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: The light formula contains minimal added sugars, helping to maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Includes vitamin D, calcium, and magnesium to support bone health and neuromuscular function.

items.title: Improved digestibility
items.content: Protease and lactase enzymes aid faster and more complete nutrient absorption.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Glutamine and antioxidants help strengthen the immune system after intense workouts.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Contains whey protein, which may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with dairy sensitivities.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: Overconsumption can strain the kidneys, especially in people with pre‑existing kidney conditions.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: The light version may use sucralose or stevia, which some consumers prefer to avoid.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High calcium levels can affect the absorption of certain antibiotics.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix one scoop (≈30 g) of powder with 250‑300 ml of water, milk, or a plant‑based beverage. For extra flavor and energy, add fruit, berries, or nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place, tightly sealed. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping and spoilage.

rice-white-and-wild-cooked-fat-added.title: Rice, white and wild, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Rice, white and wild, is a blend of selected long‑grain white rice and wild (also called “Zizania”) rice, prepared as a ready‑to‑eat product with added fat. The mixture has a tender texture, a subtle nutty aroma, and a mildly fatty flavor, making it a convenient side dish or base for many meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination pairs the quick energy of white rice with the higher protein and fiber content of wild rice.
Wild rice is not a true rice but an aquatic grass seed native to North America.
Adding a small amount of oil improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and makes the dish more satiating.
This ready‑made product is popular in cafeterias, cafés, and for fast home cooking.
When stored in a sealed package in a cool, dry place, it remains fresh for up to 12 months.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides fast‑acting carbohydrates that are quickly converted into energy, useful for active individuals and athletes.

items.title: Rich in protein and fiber
items.content: Wild rice contributes about 15 % protein and a notable amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The blend contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: The added fat is typically plant‑based and contains monounsaturated fatty acids that may benefit heart health.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact
items.content: Combining white and wild rice with a modest amount of fat slows sugar absorption, reducing blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the oils used in the product.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Added fat increases the calorie density, so portion control is advisable for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Arsenic in wild rice
items.content: Wild rice can accumulate trace amounts of arsenic from the soil; it is recommended to vary grain sources and not consume excessive amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cooked rice can be served as a side to meat, fish, or vegetable dishes, incorporated into salads, soups, and casseroles. It reheats well in the microwave or on a skillet with a splash of water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in its original packaging in a dry, cool place away from direct light. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and use within 3–4 days. Discard if a rancid odor develops.
